
5f-Block Double-Zeta Basis Set Archive
======================================


Date: 25 Mar 2005


When publishing work that uses these basis sets, please use the following citation:

K.G. Dyall, in preparation. Available from the Dirac web site, http://dirac.chem.sdu.dk.



This archive contains the exponents and the SCF spinor or orbital coefficients, 
given with respect to normalized (spherical or 2-spinor) Gaussian functions, for
the double-zeta basis sets described in the above article.  The contractions
are taken from SCF calculations on a weighted average of the valence configurations:

* For Ac, Pa, U, Np, Cm, and Lr, where the 6d is occupied in the ground state, the
5f^n-1 6d^1 7s^2, and 5f^n-1 7p^1 7s^2 configurations were used with a 100:6 weight ratio.
Note that for Ac the 5f is empty: this element is treated as a transition metal.

* For Th, the 6d^2 7s^2, 5f^1 6d^1 7s^2 and  6d^1 7s^2 7p^1 configurations were used,
with a weight ratio of 100:10:6

* For the rest (Pu, Am, Cf - No), the 5f^n 7s^2,5f^n-1 6d^1 7s^2, and 5f^n-1 7p^1 7s^2
configurations were used with a weight ratio of 100:10:6

The archive is set out as follows.

1. Exponents and SCF coefficients for Dirac-Hartree-Fock wave functions, in order
   of Z. The large component functions are given first, followed by the small 
   component functions. Both components are labelled with the large component
   symmetry type, but the primitive functions for the small component are
   those obtained by restricted kinetic balance from the large component.
   The spin-orbit components have a "-" label for j=l-1/2 and a "+" label for
   j=l+1/2.

2. Exponents and SCF coefficients for spin-free modified Dirac-Hartree-Fock wave
   functions, in order of Z. The large component functions are given first, 
   followed by the pseudo-large component functions, then the Foldy-Wouthuysen
   transformed large component functions. Note that all components have the same
   symmetry type. 

3. Exponents of correlating functions for the 5f shell, the 6d and 7s shells, 
   and the 5d shell.

4. Exponents of polarizing functions for the 5f shell and for the 6d and 7s shells.



Basis set construction.
----------------------

Contracted basis sets can be constructed by adding primitive functions to the SCF 
set. These basis sets are described below. Note that the term "douple zeta" applies 
to the s and p set. The d set is triple zeta, and the f set is quadruple zeta. This 
is a result of keeping a reasonable energy balance for the basis sets. The general
rule is that shells with l>1 require an extra function, and the second shell for a 
given l requires an extra function. 

NOTE: Functions are counted from the function with the smallest exponent to the largest. 


1. Valence. The valence space is split into two spatial regions, the outer containing
   the 6d, 7s, and 7p, and the inner containing the 5f, 6s, and 6p. The uncontracted
   functions for these two sets are described separately. However, because all these 
   shells are active or semi-active, the description below should be regarded as a 
   single contracted set. 5f flexibility is not included for Ac, which is a transition
   metal, but it is included for Th because the 5f is low-lying. 

   To the SCF functions, add the following primitives.

   For 6d/7s/7p flexibility: 
   2nd s primitive from the SCF set 
   2nd p primitive from the SCF set 
   1st d primitive from the SCF set 
   correlating f or even-tempered f except for Th: (1st f primitive from the SCF set)

   For 5f/6s/6p flexibility: 
   4th s primitive from the SCF set
   4th p primitive from the SCF set 
   3rd d primitive from the SCF set
   1st and 2nd f primitive from the SCF set, except for Ac (no f functions)  
   correlating g function for the 5f shell, except for Ac.

   The combined set is therefore:
   2nd and 4th s primitives from the SCF set 
   2nd and 4th p primitives from the SCF set
   1st and 3rd d primitives from the SCF set
   1st and 2nd f primitives from the SCF set, and the even-tempered extension
   Correlating g function for the 5f shell, except for Ac.


   If linear dependence is encountered in the d set, omit the 2nd d, or delete the 6d 
   SCF function. 

   (HF + 2s2p2d3f1g)

2. Valence + 5d correlation.  This set adds functions for correlating the 5d. 
   Excitations from the 5d into the 5f shell are important for correlating the 5f. 

   To basis set 1, add the following:
   6th s primitive from the SCF set
   6th p primitive from the SCF set 
   6th d primitive from the SCF set 
   4th f primitive from the SCF set 

   (HF + 3s3p5d4f1g)

3. Dipole polarization of the 5f. Add the polarizing g function. 

   NOTE: The polarizing g function plays an important role in the actinyls at the SCF level: 
   it changes the bond length and the harmonic frequencies. Therefore, the minimum basis
   set should include this function. Th is included because the 5f plays a role in ThO2.
 
4. Dipole polarization of the 6d. Add the polarizing f function. 

   NOTE: This function is close to the correlating f function for the early actinides,
   except for Th, where the correlating f is much tighter. You might not need the polarizing
   f until the later part of the series; and in any case, accurate polarizabilities will not
   be obtained with a double-zeta basis set. 





Dirac-Hartree-Fock basis sets           
=============================
